Choose where recordings are saved. Internal keeps them on this device; USB uses removable storage; NAS or explicitly enabled FTP saves them to a local network server. Plain FTP is unencrypted. All still play back here.
Synology, a shared Windows folder, or any SMB2/3 server
A drive plugged into this device (formatted exFAT or FAT32)
Private IPv4 server on your local network only
Plain FTP does not encrypt the username, password, or video. Other devices on the network may capture them. Never use a public network or an Internet server.

For safety, FullTV accepts only a numeric private IPv4 address (10.x, 172.16–31.x, or 192.168.x). Hostnames, DNS, and public IP addresses are blocked. FTP is only a recording destination. The folder is relative to the FTP account root (for example, FullTV/Recordings); leave it blank to use the root.

Find FTP services advertised on this network or use the current router address. Many routers do not advertise FTP. The other device must have an FTP server enabled with write access. After filling a field, press Next on the keyboard to continue; the page scrolls to keep focus visible.
Searching the local network for FTP servers…
No advertised FTP server was found. Enable an FTP server on the computer/router, use the router shortcut, or enter its private IPv4 address.
Could not search the local network. You can still enter a private IPv4 address manually.

I understand and accept unencrypted transfer

Check the FTP settings. Use a numeric private IPv4 address and a relative folder path, or leave the folder blank to use the account root.

Your provider\'s guide is used automatically. If it\'s empty — many are — turn on a free guide for your country and channels are matched to it by name.

Guide URLs are detected anywhere in an M3U. Every unique guide found is added and enabled automatically. Playlists with many regions can use substantial network and storage; pause feeds you do not need in Settings. Plain HTTP guide URLs are blocked for privacy; use HTTPS where available.
This guide does not use HTTPS, which FullTV requires. Change it to an HTTPS URL; the previous guide stays available until a successful update.
Pause and clear extra M3U guides?

This disables feeds discovered in M3U playlists and removes only their stored guide entries. The first guide for each playlist, channels, favourites and recordings are kept. You can enable a feed again later.

Optimization never deletes recordings. Recordings on USB or NAS are not included in the app-private file count.

This removes guide programmes outside the retained date window and compacts the database. Channels, favourites, settings and recordings are not deleted. The operation can take a while and needs free space.

Copy your continue-watching history between two FullTV devices over your own Wi-Fi using pinned HTTPS — nothing leaves the house, and no account is involved.
On the other FullTV: Settings → Sync → Receive, and enter:
Compare this 24-character code on both TVs. The receiving FullTV checks it before sending the six-digit access code or requesting any data.
This device will share its watch history for a few minutes, behind a code.
Type address#code#TLS code shown on the other device
Sync favourites, watch history and NAS recordings between all your devices through your own NAS. No server, no account.
Set up your NAS under Settings → Recording first, then come back here.
Saved this device to the NAS. No other devices have synced here yet.
Some devices use a different sync group. Pair each device once through HTTPS sync using its address, six-digit code and TLS pin; then retry NAS sync.
Couldn\'t reach your NAS. Check it\'s on and the details in Recording settings are right.

Export a password-encrypted file to move sources, credentials, settings, favourites and watch history to another device. Keep the passphrase separate. Video recordings and cached catalogues are not copied; restored sources are refreshed over the internet. USB folder permissions must be chosen again on the new device.

Configuration and playback metadata only: recorded video files are not included. Local/USB recordings must be copied separately; NAS recordings remain on the NAS. Choose the USB folder again after restoring.
Backup passphrase (12+ to export; 8+ for older backups)

Updates are published with the FullTV project releases.

A free, open-source IPTV player for Android TV, Fire TV and phones. It\'s a player only — it doesn\'t supply channels; you connect the service you already pay for. Nothing you enter leaves your device except to talk to your own provider.

FullTV is developed openly, with AI doing a large share of the coding under human direction — that\'s stated plainly, not hidden. Because it\'s open source, no single person going away can take it down: anyone can read every line, build it, and carry it on.

FullTV is free and always will be — nothing is gated. If it\'s useful and you\'d like to chip in, GitHub Sponsors or a one-off tip keeps the updates coming: new features, fixes and support all come out of spare evenings. Entirely optional, and genuinely appreciated.
Report a bug / request a feature

FullTV accepts HTTPS addresses only. HTTP and other URL schemes are blocked; if your provider does not offer HTTPS, this source is not supported.

The MAC your provider tied to your line, e.g. 00:1A:79:xx:xx:xx.
